newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso prime minister resigns.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso prime minister resigns.

text.p: Burkina Faso's prime minister, Kadre Desire Ouedraogo, and his government resigned on Friday after he and 17 other members of the government won national assembly seats in the May 11 parliamentary election.
Under the West African nation's constitution a member of the national assembly cannot serve in government.
Ouedraogo was one of 97 members of President Blaise Compaore's ruling Congress for Democracy and Progress (CDP) who won seats in the new assembly. The assembly has 111 seats.
Compaore's party held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992 during the former French colony's return to multi-party politics.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111 and allow Compaore to stand as many times as he wants for president.
The constitution initially limited him to one seven-year term. The next presidential election is due in 1998.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 army coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.
